description: A plain world: only Fabric API and Quicksilver. Coordinates assume nothing about the world but its seed (CI uses 12345).

scenes.title: World spawn of seed 12345, 8 chunks, daylight (fixed camera height above the terrain)
Fly-through over fresh terrain, 12 chunks, scripted path north at 10 blocks/s
scenes.ciNote: Against the committed baselines CI gates only memory here: upload volume and draw calls depend on how fast CI's server generates the new terrain. Its draw calls are gated against vanilla measured in the same run (package 3).

scenes.ciVanillaDrawGateReason: Its average follows the runner's frame rate: below 20 fps every frame lines up with a game tick and draws the tick's extra draws, above it some don't. run 40180107484 attempt 2, Vulkan: Quicksilver 124.0 average / 124 median at 18.57 fps, vanilla's measure run 103.78 / 124 at 24.15 fps. Gated against vanilla on the median (Andre's rule, 2026-10-25).

scenes.title: The crosshair's block outline round a stone block on a smooth stone floor (package 7)
setup: item replace entity @a weapon.mainhand with minecraft:air
scenes.ciNote: CI's pin mod leaves the crosshair's block outline out of every scene (it moves by a pixel row between frames on GL 3.3, in vanilla's runs too) except round this scene's stone block at 2680 200 -1988, so the outline is still checked here (package 7). Creative mode, as the game draws no outline in spectator; the bare shot is the same view in adventure mode (no outline round a block the empty hand cannot break; hearts and food shown), to measure what the outline covers.

scenes.title: Mobs, chests, a banner and signs behind a stone wall and under a stone floor, some seen through a glass window, a doorway and a glass floor (package 2)
scenes.ciNote: Quicksilver must hide some entities and block entities here (the ones the wall and the floor cover); the pixel gates catch any it hides wrongly (the ones seen through glass and the doorway).

scenes.title: The occlusion layout with the camera sliding along the wall at 0.8 blocks/s while a pig is moved in and out of view and part of the wall is opened and closed again (package 2)
scenes.ciNote: Moving pass: objects are hidden and come into view as the camera passes the window and doorway, as a pig is moved and as the wall opens. The per-frame ray check covers every frame of the bench; ciShots compare fixed points with vanilla under both gates (the bare_* shots, with every object removed, measure each object's on-screen area). Counts against the committed baselines: memory only (the mid-bench commands upload new meshes).; draw calls are gated against vanilla measured in the same run (package 3).

scenes.title: Package 2b: the camera slides east past the corner of a large building on a sky platform at 2 blocks/s while turning to look behind it, where rows of walls (and the terrain under the platform) are hidden and then revealed
scenes.ciNote: Package 2b's turning-the-corner check: sections behind the building are culled and come into view as the camera passes the corner and turns; CI's occlusion check covers every frame, ciShots compare fixed points along the path with vanilla. Counts against the committed baselines: memory only (the camera reveals new sections all the time); draw calls are gated against vanilla measured in the same run.

scenes.title: Water in a glass tank, a wall of stained glass in stripes of six colours, ice and glass panes, with the camera sliding past at 1.5 blocks/s (package 3)
scenes.ciNote: Moving pass: vanilla re-sorts the translucent sections as the camera crosses blocks; Quicksilver must draw every one of them in vanilla's order with vanilla's latest sort (checked every frame of the bench). ciShots compare fixed points with vanilla under both gates, taken after the camera has moved there; 'back' returns to the start after the other points, and 'bare_back' (the single ice block in front of the stripes removed) measures the smallest translucent element's area on screen. Counts against the committed baselines: memory only (the moving camera makes vanilla re-sort and upload new index lists).; draw calls are gated against vanilla measured in the same run (package 3).

scenes.title: Water, ice and stained glass in a glass tank, with Improved Transparency (package 3)
Water in a glass tank, a wall of stained glass in stripes of six colours, ice and glass panes, with the camera sliding past at 1.5 blocks/s with Improved Transparency (package 3)
scenes.ciNote: The translucent_move scene with Improved Transparency: vanilla does not sort translucent terrain then (its order-independent passes need no order), so neither does Quicksilver; it draws each stage with the pipeline made from vanilla's for that stage.

scenes.ciVanillaDrawGateReason: Its average follows the runner's frame rate: the slower a run, the more of its frames line up with a game tick and draw that tick's extra draws, so the average moves with fps while the median does not. run 40274749083, Vulkan: Quicksilver 121.34 average / 124 median at 20.36 fps, vanilla's measure run 103.03 / 124 at 24.41 fps (limit x 1.10 + 2: 115.33); full on the same run: 123.96 / 124 against 123.62 / 124 at 15.72 and 16.15 fps. Gated against vanilla on the median (Andre's rule, 2026-10-25).
scenes.title: A garden of plants with smooth lighting off (flat lighting): grass, ferns, flowers, berry bushes, saplings, pink petals, crops on farmland, sugar cane and lily pads by water, leaves, bamboo, azaleas, moss carpet and vines (package 4)
scenes.ciNote: Flat lighting of cross and angled plant models (package 4: Quicksilver lights blocks exactly as Indigo, the vanilla runs' renderer, does, flat lighting included). Random ticks are stopped so nothing grows, spreads or dries out. The gamerule stays at 0 for the rest of that game's server, in every run alike (the later sessions: renderer_off and the Improved Transparency scenes).

scenes.ciVanillaDrawGateReason: Its average follows the runner's frame rate: the slower a run, the more of its frames line up with a game tick and draw that tick's extra draws, so the average moves with fps while the median does not. run 40279156080, Vulkan: Quicksilver 96.3 average / 123 median at 25.89 fps, vanilla's measure run 84.85 / 123 at 29.76 fps (limit x 1.10 + 2: 95.34); full on the same run: 95.72 / 123 against 97.05 / 123. scenes.title: A stone-brick hut with slabs, stairs, a glass window and a block display, with Quicksilver's block renderer switched off in its config and smooth lighting off (package 4)
scenes.ciNote: CI's check of Quicksilver's block-renderer=off config option (package 4): this scene's session starts with it off (ci/client-run.sh writes config/quicksilver.properties), so every block and item, the block display included, is drawn by vanilla's own code; the pictures are gated against the vanilla runs like every scene's. Smooth lighting is off because vanilla's own smooth lighting is not Indigo's (Indigo's flat lighting of these cube-shaped blocks is vanilla's). Besides the picture, CI checks the bench's renderer report in this session: no block and no API mesh quad went Quicksilver's way, and blocks went vanilla's (in every other session, no block went vanilla's). The self-test checks, quad by quad, that this vanilla path hands vanilla's output on unchanged for tinted, cutout and light-emitting blocks.

scenes.title: About 65 kinds of particle at fixed places 3 blocks in front of the camera, before a stone wall, the same in every run (package 8)
scenes.ciNote: The CI pin mod (ci/pin-mod, Pins) makes every particle made in this area the same in every run, vanilla and Quicksilver alike: its random numbers come from where and what it is, it is not ticked and is drawn at partial tick 0 while the player is here, and it is removed when the player leaves. The bench sets the scene up again after the bare shot has removed the first set, so it measures one of each particle too. The 'bare' shot steps out of the area and back, so the pin removes every particle: the same view without them, which measures each particle's area on screen.

scenes.title: Animated blocks in front of the camera and 34 blocks behind it, with animation run for a fixed number of ticks in every run (package 8)
scenes.ciNote: The CI pin mod (ci/pin-mod, Pins) sends every animated texture back to its first frame when the player enters this area, lets it run exactly 70 texture ticks (one per frame that runs a client tick) and holds it, in every run, vanilla and Quicksilver alike. Everything here is built after those ticks, so Quicksilver left every changed sprite out and must redraw each one before it is drawn: the front blocks when their sections first show, the block particle (a command block sprite seen nowhere else) on its first use outside terrain, and the blocks 34 blocks behind the camera (other sprites, two sections behind it, outside vanilla's visible sections) when the 'behind' shot turns around and walks there. During the bench a marker block under the floor lets animation run freely (vanilla's animation work against Quicksilver's); its screenshots are taken before that. While measuring, its steps check the module's three catch-up paths again with animation running: a block particle of the chain command block (a sprite only the far blocks show, so stale) at 4 s, and a repeating command block facing the camera (its front sprite only on the far blocks) at 8 s; compare.py requires sprites left out, a redraw before terrain and a redraw on first use inside the measured window.
scenes.ciDrawCallGateReason: While measuring, animation runs freely: vanilla redraws changed sprites once per client tick, so the per-frame average follows the runner's frame rate (more frames per tick, fewer draws per frame) while the draws per tick stay the same. Run 40267202902, full: average 33.35, median 44 at 30 fps. Gated on the median from the start (Andre's rule for such scenes, design doc, Testing).

scenes.title: Animated block sprites outside terrain: a hotbar with a magma block, a sea lantern, prismarine and buckets, an item frame and a block display with a magma block, a burning cow; animation run a fixed number of ticks (package 8)
setup: item replace entity @a hotbar.0 with minecraft:magma_block
item replace entity @a hotbar.1 with minecraft:sea_lantern
item replace entity @a hotbar.2 with minecraft:prismarine
item replace entity @a hotbar.3 with minecraft:lava_bucket
item replace entity @a hotbar.4 with minecraft:water_bucket
scenes.ciDrawCallGateReason: While measuring, animation runs freely (as in the animation scene): vanilla redraws changed sprites once per client tick, so the per-frame average follows the runner's frame rate. Gated on the median from the start (Andre's rule for such scenes).
scenes.ciNote: Andre's follow-up for package 8: every animated block sprite here is shown only outside terrain (the hotbar and the held block, the item frame, the block display, the fire on the cow), so each is redrawn by Quicksilver on its first use outside terrain. The CI pin mod sends every animated texture back to frame 0 when the player enters this area, runs 70 texture ticks and holds it, in every run, vanilla and Quicksilver alike; everything is placed after those ticks, so every one of those sprites is stale at its first use. CI fails on any late redraw (here and in every scene). During the bench a marker block under the floor lets animation run freely; its screenshot is taken before that. The player is in creative mode here (for the hotbar); the next scenes set spectator again.

scenes.title: Package 6: a base full of block entities: chests of every kind (single, double, trapped, ender, copper), shulker boxes, standing, wall and hanging signs with text, heads, decorated pots, a bell, beds, standing and wall banners with patterns
scenes.ciNote: Package 6's block entities against vanilla's renderers (the entity atlas, and baking). CI's pin mod holds this area's banners at a swayed pose fixed by each banner's position (running with the game time during the bench, after the step at 0.5 s sets the marker block under the floor), so the banners are checked away from rest. Extra shots: four lids opened by /qscichest (a single and a double chest, an ender chest, a shulker box; open after the 3 s wait, resting open), two signs' text changed with /data, then the lids closed again (resting closed).
